Seminar Title:

Physical, Mechanical and Wear Properties of Additively Manufactured AlSi10Mg Alloy Parts

Seminar Type:

Sandhyarani Biswas

Abstract:

Additive manufacturing (AM) of aluminum (Al) alloys is a promising technique for producing lightweight components with superior mechanical properties, making it ideal for weight-sensitive applications such as automotive and aerospace industries. AlSi10Mg is one of the most suitable feed stock materials for metal AM, especially for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) process, due to its exceptional printability, high strength-to-weight ratio, and excellent melt fluidity. The objective of the present work is to study the mechanical and wear behavior of LPBF based 3D printed AlSi10Mg alloy at different parameter settings. AlSi10Mg alloy parts are successfully fabricated using LPBF based AM process. Experiments are conducted based on Taguchi's L9 orthogonal array design. The process parameters like laser power (170 W, 270 W and 370 W), scan speed (900 mm/s, 1100 mm/s and 1300 mm/s), layer thickness (0.02 mm, 0.025 mm and 0.03 mm), and hatch spacing (0.09 mm, 0.14 mm and 0.19 mm) are considered for optimization. The spherical morphology of the AlSi10Mg powder particles, as confirmed by SEM, is expected to enhance both powder flowability and packing density during LPBF. Consequently, this optimized powder bed quality can improve the mechanical and wear properties of the fabricated components. The chemical composition of the AlSi10Mg alloy is verified using EDX analysis. The presence of elements in AlSi10Mg alloy observed as peaks of Al, Si, Mg, Ti and Fe by EDX spectrum. The aim of the current research work is to study the effect of LPBF laser power, scan speed, layer thickness, and hatch spacing on the mechanical and wear properties of the as-built part. The effect of sliding wear parameters such as sliding distance, normal load and sliding speed on the wear behavior of 3D printed parts will be studied. A comparative study on the mechanical and wear behavior of AlSi10Mg parts made by AM and conventional powder metallurgy process will also be done. Finally, the surface morphology of fractured and worn surfaces will be analyzed using SEM.
